extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, OED staff, and USPTO counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for imposing reciprocal discipline on a registered patent practitioner under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 (including notice/service rules, opportunity to respond, grounds for reciprocal suspension, and the specific obligations and prohibitions imposed as discipline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary authority of the USPTO to impose reciprocal discipline derives from statute (35 U.S.C. § 32) and the cited regulations; decisions are published and available in the OED Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for imposition of reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may request imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by a duly constituted authority of a State (e.g., suspension) unless the respondent establishes one or more of the reasons in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1) to oppose identical imposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the Supreme Court of Illinois based on reasons in 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and notice requirements (publication and certified mail)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must attempt service (e.g., certified mail); if unsuccessful, the Notice and Order may be published in the Official Gazette to effect notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Here, after unsuccessful attempts to deliver via certified mail, the OED Director published the Notice and Order in the Official Gazette; the published notice must inform the respondent of the proceeding and the 40-day response window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond and consequences of non-response
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is given forty (40) days to file a response opposing imposition of identical reciprocal discipline; failure to file a response permits a determination that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this matter, Respondent did not file a response, and consequently it was determined there was no genuine issue of material fact and reciprocal suspension was appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicate misconduct supporting suspension (as described in state order)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Illinois suspension was for failing to act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client, failing to keep a client reasonably informed about the status of a matter, failing to refund the unearned portion of the client's fee, and failing to cooperate with the Illinois Attorney Registration and Disciplinary Commission's investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal discipline may be predicated upon the respondent's state-court or state-discipline findings of professional misconduct; the USPTO suspension here is explicitly "predicated upon being suspended from the practice of law for one year by a duly constituted authority of a State."

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition of identical discipline (suspension from practice before USPTO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from the practice of patent, trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO for one year, effective the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reciprocal discipline is ordered identical to the state-imposed discipline, the USPTO's suspension covers practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters for the same term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to publish Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette containing the name of the practitioner, registration number, the disciplinary action (suspension for one year), the regulatory provision violated (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)), and the predicate state action and reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice should state the practitioner’s registration number, domicile, the nature and duration of the suspension, and the factual bases as stated by the state disciplinary authority; publication is part of the remedial steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This communication obligation ensures reciprocal and coordinating notification across jurisdictions and public disclosure of the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the order does not restate § 11.58, the duties typically include obligations such as notifying clients, ceasing to represent clients before the Office, and taking steps to protect client interests while suspended; the practitioner must follow those regulatory duties during the suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure ("PKI") certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative action will remove the practitioner’s ability to file electronically or be listed on existing customer accounts while suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to a USPTO Customer Number until reinstated
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall he have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This bar prevents the practitioner from circumventing the suspension by obtaining filing privileges through customer numbers or certificate access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of disciplinary decisions to the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are available for public reading at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication and public access to disciplinary decisions serve transparency and public notice purposes.
